question: What does published evidence say about the main causal pathways through which greater English devolution could affect local decision-making, integration and prevention, public-service performance, fiscal incentives, growth, accountability, fairness and system stewardship?

scope.populationContext: Subnational and local government, prioritising England and OECD settings; wider international evidence used where it informs mechanisms and is explicitly labelled indirect.
scope.interventionsExposures: Political, administrative and fiscal decentralisation; local fiscal autonomy; integrated/place-based service governance; transparency and accountability; institutional capacity; equalisation and national stewardship.
scope.comparators: More centralised arrangements, alternative decentralisation designs, pre-reform periods, or cross-jurisdiction variation depending on study design.
scope.outcomes: Decision responsiveness, coordination, prevention, service efficiency and quality, accountability, public investment, growth, fiscal equity and implementation capability.
scope.time: No strict publication-date cut-off; emphasis on high-value reviews, evaluations and current English institutional evidence.

inclusion: Peer-reviewed empirical studies and evidence reviews relevant to a defined pathway
Official evaluations and audit reports with transparent methods
High-quality international synthesis from OECD, World Bank and comparable institutions
English fiscal analyses that directly assess distributional or incentive mechanisms
exclusion: Commentary used as evidence of effect
Unverified claims or inaccessible sources where key study details could not be checked
Purely normative arguments without empirical or institutional evidence
searchApproach: Targeted rapid searches across GOV.UK, NAO, OECD, IFS, World Bank, academic publisher/repository pages and citation-linked literature. Searches deliberately sought positive, null and contradictory evidence. Each source included in the database was checked against an accessible publisher, repository or official page.

screeningAccount.note: This is a rapid, decision-focused search rather than a systematic review. Search results were screened iteratively by pathway and stopped when additional searches were mainly returning duplicates, lower-relevance commentary or studies already represented by stronger syntheses. Counts are not presented as PRISMA counts because the search interfaces used did not expose reliable deduplicated corpus totals.

appraisal: Evidence is rated against relevance, identification/design strength, directness to the pathway, consistency, caveats and transferability. Body-of-evidence confidence is reported as strong, moderate, developing or limited. These labels are public-facing translations of standard evidence-confidence concepts and are not derived from unpublished guidance.
shortcutsAndBias: Database coverage is not exhaustive and paywalled literature may be under-represented.
The review prioritises syntheses and decision-relevant English evidence rather than extracting every primary study within each review.
International evidence is used for mechanisms only where English direct evidence is weak; transferability is explicitly caveated.
Sector-specific prevention and culture/sport pathways require dedicated follow-up REAs.
